prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S136: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages accepted bags for onward processing without changing their flight association.
S137: Induction Tray Conveyor meters bags into the handling stream at a rate that avoids accumulation at the make-up interface.
S138: Primary Crossbelt Sorter separates bags according to their authorized destination and current operating status.
S139: North Gate Scanner verifies readable bag identification before bags proceed toward their assigned build.
S140: South Gate Scanner provides the corresponding verification for bags processed in its coverage area.
S141: Image Resolution Desk uses the exception ticket to confirm an authorized make-up position for an oversize bag.
S142: Secondary Inspection Chute retains bags requiring further examination until the applicable disposition is recorded.
S143: Bag Reconciliation Station uses the Late Transfer Bag Card to reconcile a transfer bag against its intended flight.
S144: Transfer Bag Feeder meters accepted transfer bags into the active handling sequence without bypassing required checks.
S145: East Make-Up Conveyor delivers assigned bags to the designated make-up position at a controlled rate.
S146: West Make-Up Conveyor provides the equivalent delivery function for positions in its operating area.
S147: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit maintains bag order and position information for its active flight build.
S148: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit receives the Carousel Release Slip only after its position and flight assignment have been checked.
S149: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms staffing, equipment availability, and the planned loading sequence before accepting a build for loading.
S150: Outbound Load Control Desk reconciles the completed build against the permitted flight load before departure closeout.
S151: Bag Tag Printer produces replacement identification only when authorized personnel have confirmed the required bag details.
S152: Security Duty Manager resolves release holds that require a security decision before bags can enter a departure build.
S153: Maintenance Technician reports equipment restrictions that affect lane availability or safe bag delivery.
S154: Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates changes to build priority with airline ground operations and communicates any resulting delivery constraints.
S155: Manual resolution begins when an image or identity exception prevents automatic processing from establishing a reliable disposition.
S156: Image Resolution Desk presents the available bag image and exception details to the operator for review.
S157: The operator compares visible bag features with the recorded tag number and the handling data associated with the bag.
S158: The operator confirms that the image is legible enough to support a decision and does not rely on an uncertain visual match.
S159: Image Resolution Desk uses the rescan receipt to confirm that a second image was captured under the approved procedure.
S160: When the image remains inconclusive, the operator requests a physical inspection through the established inspection process.
S161: The identity check verifies that the physical tag is attached to the inspected bag and that its number agrees with the recorded bag identity.
S162: Baggage Control System checks the recorded bag identity against the current routing data before any disposition is committed.
S163: Flight Data Gateway provides the flight data used to validate the bag's assigned destination and service date.
S164: Bag Reconciliation Station records whether the inspected bag matches the expected flight assignment.
S165: A mismatch places the bag on hold until an authorized operator resolves the discrepancy or escalates it.
S166: Juniper holds the affected bag from automatic sorting while the manual disposition remains unresolved.
S167: Kestrel captures a readable tag image when the bag is presented for a permitted scan.
S168: North Gate Scanner records the tag read and image data needed to support an operator's identity check.
S169: Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled location for bags requiring physical examination.
S170: Explosives Response Team conducts any security examination assigned under applicable procedures.
S171: Baggage Operations Supervisor approves the operational disposition when the case exceeds the operator's authority.
S172: After the identity and flight checks pass, Baggage Control System authorizes the bag to rejoin its previously assigned screening and sort path.
S173: Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the bag remains eligible for inclusion in the planned flight load.
S174: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms any flight-side constraint that could prevent the reconciled bag from being accepted.
S175: Concourse Zone Controller applies the authorized routing state without bypassing required screening controls.
S176: Maintenance Technician uses the witness tag to verify that the applicable calibration status was witnessed before equipment returns to service.
S177: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.
S178: The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
S179: Safe operation depends on keeping people clear of moving equipment and maintaining a controlled path for every bag.
S180: The Baggage Operations Supervisor may stop induction when an unsafe condition, uncertain bag location, or loss of control is reported.
S181: A stop command places the affected equipment in a defined safe state without disabling unrelated routes that remain safe to operate.
